NONE: › perfectly clean or tidy
潔淨的，整潔的
› perfect and without any mistakes
完美的

example: dressed in an immaculate white suit
身穿潔白的套裝
an immaculate garden
潔淨的花園
He gave an immaculate performance as the aging hero.
他完美地扮演了那個年邁的英雄。

NONE: › present as a natural and permanent part of something
內在的

example: an immanent God
內心的上帝

NONE: › not important, or not relating to the subject you are thinking about
不重要的，無關緊要的

example: Whether the book is well or badly written is immaterial (to me) - it has an important message.
（我覺得）這本書寫得是好是壞並不重要——它給了我們一個重要的啟示。

NONE: C2 disapproving not behaving in a way that is as calm and wise as people expect from someone of your age
不成熟的
› disapproving not having much experience of something
沒經驗的
› specialized biology not yet completely grown or developed
未長成的，發育未全的

example: Stop being so silly and immature, Chris!
克裡斯，不要這麼愚蠢幼稚！
She's rather immature for her age, don't you think?
她都這麼大了，你不覺得她顯得相當幼稚嗎？
politically immature
政治上不夠老練
While the animals are still immature, they do not breed.
動物發育未全時不會生育。

NONE: › so large or great that it cannot be measured or known exactly
不可估量的，無限的

example: Her movies had an immeasurable effect on a generation of Americans.
她的影片對一代美國人有著無法估量的影響。

NONE: › the fact that something seems real and important, so that you feel involved with it
即時性；直接性

example: Pre-recorded TV programmes have so much less immediacy and warmth than live theatre.
事先錄製的電視節目比劇院現場少了很多的即時性和親切感。

NONE: B2 happening or done without delay or very soon after something else
立即的，立刻的
C1 used to refer to something or someone that is close to, or is a cause of or an effect of, something or someone else
接近的，緊接的，直接的
B2 in the present or as soon as possible
目前的；盡快的
› the period of time that is coming next
近期
› your closest relations, such as your parents, children, husband, or wife
直系親屬（如父母、子女、配偶等）

example: We must make an immediate response.
我們必須立即作出反應。
Dioxin is a poison that takes immediate effect.
二噁英是一種速效毒藥。
There are few facilities in the immediate area.
在鄰近地區幾乎沒有甚麼設施。
An immediate result/effect of the war was a breakdown of law and order.
戰爭的直接後果／影響是法治的癱瘓。
We have no immediate plans.
我們目前沒有計劃。
The public has demanded his immediate resignation.
公眾要他立刻辭職。

NONE: A2 now or without waiting or thinking
立即，馬上
C1 close to something or someone in distance or time
（距離或時間上）接近，緊接
› closely or directly
緊接地；直接地
› as soon as
一…就

example: We really ought to leave immediately.
我們真的應該馬上就走。
The purpose of the meeting wasn't immediately obvious.
會議的目的並不十分明確。
Milton Street is on the left, immediately after the bank.
密爾頓大街在左邊，一過銀行就是。
They moved in immediately before Christmas.
他們在聖誕節前不久才搬進來。
We heard a loud crash from the room immediately above us.
我們聽到從正上方的房間傳來了一聲巨響。
The people most immediately affected by the drought are the farmers themselves.
受旱災影響最直接的是農民自己。
Immediately she'd gone, the boys started to mess about.
她一走開，那些男孩就鬧成一團。
I'll call you immediately I hear anything.
我一有甚麼消息就給你打電話。

NONE: › for a very long time
從很早開始，自古以來
› formal existing or traditional for an extremely long time
年代久遠的，古老的

example: Her family had farmed that land since time immemorial.
她的家族從很早開始就在那塊土地上耕耘了。
She said it was the immemorial custom of the villagers to have a feast after the harvesting.
她說村民在收割之後舉行宴會是一個古老的風俗。

NONE: C1 extremely large in size or degree
巨大的，無限的
› slang extremely good
非常好，極好

example: They spent an immense amount of time getting the engine into perfect condition.
他們花了大量時間使引擎運轉完美。
He's an immense goalkeeper.
他是一名非常出色的守門員。

NONE: C1 extremely
非常，極其

example: He was immensely popular in his day.
在他那個時代，他非常受歡迎。
She's an immensely talented young athlete.
她是個才華洋溢的年輕運動員。

NONE: › the extremely large size of something
巨大；廣大

example: The immensity of the task is daunting.
工作量之大令人生畏。

NONE: › to become completely involved in something
埋頭做…

T: › [ T ] formal to put something or someone completely under the surface of a liquid

example: She got some books out of the library and immersed herself in Jewish history and culture.
她從圖書館借了一些書，然後沉浸於猶太歷史和文化之中。
The shells should be immersed in boiling water for two minutes.
貝類應在沸水中浸上兩分鐘。

NONE: › an electric device used for heating water
浸沒式加熱器
› seeming to surround the audience, player, etc. so that they feel completely involved in something
身臨其境的

example: an immersive theatrical experience
身臨其境的劇場體驗
The new game is more immersive.
新的遊戲更讓人身臨其境。

NONE: B2 a person who has come to a different country in order to live there permanently
（外來的）移民

example: a large immigrant population
龐大的外來移民人口
Illegal immigrants are sent back across the border if they are caught.
非法移民如果被抓住就會從邊境被遣返。

NONE: › to come to live in a different country
（外來的）移民

example: He immigrated with his parents in 1895 and grew up on Long Island.
1895年，他與父母一起移民，並在長島長大。

NONE: B2 the act of someone coming to live in a different country
移民（入境）
B1 the process of examining your passport and other documents to make certain that you can be allowed to enter the country, or the place where this is done
移民局入境檢查；移民局入境檢查處

example: There are strict limits on immigration (into the country).
（該國）對入境移民有著嚴格的限制。
After you've been through immigration (control), you can go and get your luggage.
通過移民局入境檢查之後，你就可以去取行李了。

NONE: C2 coming or likely to happen very soon
臨近的，即將發生的

example: A strike is imminent.
一場罷工即將來臨。

NONE: › An immiscible liquid cannot be mixed with another liquid without separating from it.
不能混合的，不互溶的（液體）

example: Oil is immiscible with/in water.
油和水互不相溶。
Compare
miscible

NONE: › not moving or not able to move
靜止的；無法移動的

example: She sat immobile, wondering what to do next.
她一動不動地坐著，尋思著下一步該怎麼辦。

NONE: › to stop something or someone from moving
鎖止

example: You can immobilize the car by removing the spark plugs.
你拔去火花塞就能使汽車不能開動。
The broken limb must be immobilized as soon as possible.
已摔斷的四肢應該盡快固定住。

NONE: › a device fitted to a car that stops it from moving so that it cannot be stolen
汽車防盜器
› too much or many, or more than is usual or reasonable
過度的；不合理的；極端的
› having too high an opinion of yourself
自負的，不謙虛的
› showing too much of the body
過分暴露身體的

example: He makes these immodest statements of his own brilliance.
他說了這些自負的話，誇獎自己的聰明才智。
showing an immodest amount of leg
過分暴露大腿

NONE: › to kill yourself or someone else, or to destroy something, usually by burning, in a formal ceremony
（通常指透過焚燒）將…作為祭品殺死（或毀滅）
B2 morally wrong, or outside society's standards of acceptable, honest, and moral behaviour
不道德的，道德敗壞的
› money earned from prostitution (= having sex in exchange for money)
B2 morally wrong, or outside society's standards of acceptable, honest, and moral behaviour
不道德的，道德敗壞的
› money earned from prostitution (= having sex in exchange for money)

example: an immoral act
不道德的舉動
It's an immoral tax, because the poor will pay relatively more.
這是不道德的稅收，因為窮人相對要付出更多。
Compare
amoral
moral adjective
If convicted, she could be jailed for five years for living off immoral earnings.

NONE: C2 living or lasting for ever
永生的；永存的

C: › [ C ] someone who is so famous that they are remembered for a long time after they are dead

NONE: C2 very special and famous and therefore likely to be remembered for a long time
不朽的，流芳百世的

example: The priest said he was endangering his immortal soul.
神父說他正在危及自己不朽的靈魂。
In the immortal words of Samuel Goldwyn, "Include me out."
用塞繆爾‧戈爾德溫那句不朽的名言來說就是：「把我包括在外。」
She is one of the immortals of classical opera.
她是古典歌劇不朽的演唱家之一。

NONE: › to make someone or something so famous that that person or thing is remembered for a very long time
使不朽，使名垂千古

example: Marlene Dietrich was immortalized through her roles in films like "The Blue Angel".
瑪琳‧黛德麗在《藍天使》等影片中所扮演的角色使她名傳後世。

NONE: › fixed and impossible to move
不可移動的，固定的
› used to describe a firm opinion that is impossible to change, or someone with such an opinion
堅定不移的；不可動搖的

example: The rock weighed over a ton and was completely immovable.
這塊岩石重一噸以上，根本無法移動。

NONE: › protected against a particular disease by particular substances in the blood
免疫的

after verb: C2 [ after verb ] not affected or upset by a particular type of behaviour or emotion
› [ after verb ] not able to be punished or damaged by something

example: Most people who've had chickenpox once are immune to it for the rest of their lives.
大多數出過水痘的人終生都對此病具有免疫力。
He seems to be immune to colds - he just never gets them.
他好像對感冒具有免疫力——他從不感冒。
The press had criticized her so often that in the end she had become immune (to it).
新聞界如此頻繁地批評她，以至於到最後她都（對此）變得無動於衷了。
Journalists, he insisted, must be immune (= protected) from prosecution.
他堅持新聞記者必須免受起訴。

NONE: › the reaction within the body that is caused by antigens (= foreign substances) and results in the production of antibodies that can fight disease by killing the bacteria or viruses that cause it
免疫反應（由體內的抗原引發的反應，過程中抗原製造抗體，抗體負責殺死致病的細菌或病毒，以對抗疾病）
C2 the cells and tissues in the body that make it able to protect itself against infection
免疫系統
› a condition in which the body does not have enough platelets (= very small cells in the blood that make it thicker in order to stop bleeding), often causing very small red spots to form on the skin
特發性血小板減少性紫癜，自身免疫性血小板減少性紫癜
› a situation in which you are protected against disease or from legal action
免疫；免除；豁免

example: The vaccination gives you immunity against the disease for up to six months.
注射這種疫苗會使你對這種疾病有長達六個月的免疫力。
He was granted immunity from prosecution because he confessed the names of the other spies.
他因供出了其他間諜的名字而免受起訴。

NONE: › specialized medical the process of protecting a person or animal from an infectious disease by putting a substance into the body that makes it produce antibodies (= proteins in the blood that fight disease)
免疫接種

example: mass/routine immunization
大規模／例行接種
Immunization gives people the ability to resist infection temporarily or permanently.
免疫接種可讓人可以永久或暫時地抵抗感染。
With the use of immunizations in babies, the mortality rate has dropped significantly.
開展嬰兒免疫接種以來，死亡率顯著下降了。

NONE: › specialized medical to protect a person or animal against a disease by putting a substance into the body to make it produce antibodies (= proteins in the blood that fight disease)
（通常指透過注射）使免疫

example: Children are routinely immunized against polio.
兒童例行接種小兒麻痺症疫苗。

NONE: › a condition in which a body is unable to produce enough antibodies to fight bacteria and viruses, often resulting in infection and disease
免疫缺陷
› a protein (= chemical substance) produced by the body that can destroy harmful bacteria in the body. There are five different types: IgA, IgD, IgE, IgG, and IgM
免疫球蛋白
› relating to the process of finding antigens (= substances that cause the production of antibodies) in the cells of a piece of tissue
免疫組織化學的

example: the immunohistochemical staining of tissues
對組織的免疫組織化學染色

NONE: › relating to the structure and function of the immune system (= that part of the body that fights off viruses, bacteria, fungi, and other types of infection)
免疫學的

example: A monocyte is a white blood cell that can provide immunological defences against many infectious organisms.
單核細胞是一種白細胞，可提供針對許多感染性生物的免疫抵抗能力。

NONE: › the study of how the body fights disease and infection
免疫學

› a situation in which the body's immune system is intentionally stopped from working, or is made less effective, usually by drugs, especially in order to help the body accept an organ that has been taken from another person's body
免疫抑制（通常透過藥物刻意抑制免疫反應，或令其效率降低，尤其用於減低身體對移植器官的排斥反應）

example: High levels of immunosuppression are needed to prevent rejection of transplanted tissue or organs.
需要高強度的免疫抑制來防止對移植器官或組織的排斥。

NONE: › preventing the immune system from reacting to antigens, for example in order to prevent transplanted organs from being rejected
免疫抑制的

example: While immunosuppressive drugs can help prevent rejection of transplanted tissues or organs, they can also give rise to infections.
免疫抑制藥物可以説明防止移植器官或組織被身體排斥，但是它們也會引起感染增加。

NONE: › treatment that improves ability of the immune system to fight disease
免疫治療

example: Immunotherapy with interferons may be used in patients with infections that are very difficult to treat.
使用干擾素的免疫治療可以用在感染難以治愈的病人身上。

NONE: › kept as a prisoner or closed away and out of sight
監禁的，禁閉的

example: Immured in a dark airless cell, the hostages waited six months for their release.
人質等待獲釋期間在不通風的昏暗小屋中被禁閉了六個月。

NONE: › not changing, or unable to be changed
永恆的；不可改變的

example: an immutable law
永恆的法則
Some people regard grammar as an immutable set of rules.
有些人認為文法是一套不可更改的規則。
